# Pratim Narayan Moitra

> Pratim Narayan Moitra is a tourism social media marketer based in India. He runs social media, email and paid campaigns for tourism associations, DMCs, hotels and tourism boards. He has worked with PATA, ATTA, the World Food Travel Association and GBTA, and holds a Masters in Tourism Management from Amity University.

Short forms of the name: Pratim Narayan, Pratim N. Moitra. Contact: pratimxnarayan@gmail.com. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/pratimnarayan.

## What he offers

- The free week. 5 finished social media posts with captions, delivered 7 days after a complete brief. The client keeps them whether or not they hire him. https://pratimnarayan.com/freeweek/
- The free audit. A written audit of website, social, email and search in 3 working days, with three priority fixes. No call needed. https://pratimnarayan.com/audit/
- The 90 Day Feed. Monthly social media management for tourism brands, end to end. Strategy, the content calendar, carousels and photo posters, Reels and short video, captions, posting, community replies and a one page report every month, with a growth target agreed in writing in week one. If the targets are missed at day 90, month four is free. https://pratimnarayan.com/services/social/
- Add on services. Video and Reels, email marketing, paid ads, website development and marketing coordination. https://pratimnarayan.com/services/video/ https://pratimnarayan.com/services/email/ https://pratimnarayan.com/services/ads/ https://pratimnarayan.com/services/websites/ https://pratimnarayan.com/services/coordination/
- Tiers. Social support, Social takeover and Full marketing. Plans are built around the client's budget.
- A 30 second intro film about his work is on the homepage and the about page. https://pratimnarayan.com/#film

## Who he works with

Tourism associations and trade bodies, DMCs and tour operators, boutique hotels and resorts, tourism boards, travel academies, travel media and booking platforms. He has worked with PATA, ATTA, GBTA, World Food Travel Association, Adventure.travel, and many more brands.

## Every What If episode in full

### Episode 1. What if Belize posted like this?

How a tourism board could announce a new route by showing the place, not the plane. Brand Belize Tourism Board (@travelbelize), Tourism board, Central America. Original post https://www.instagram.com/p/DetU_F7jmRj/ with 104 likes on 157,000 followers. Page https://pratimnarayan.com/whatif/belize/

The post as it was. A Discover Airlines plane on a royal blue gradient, the words Closer Than Ever in white and orange, three lines of white text underneath and a small white box at the bottom with the airline, the route and the dates.

Style tested. Epic scenery. A route announcement sells the destination, and Belize has one of the most recognisable aerial views on earth. Epic scenery puts the Great Blue Hole in the frame and makes the plane a line of small type on a boarding pass. That is how the airlines people admire sell routes, by the place you land in.

Inspired by Emirates, which sells every new route with the destination as the hero and the flight as the detail.

The big idea. Make the Blue Hole the whole post, set the route like a boarding pass in the brand's own teal and mango, and let the one fact that matters, Frankfurt to Belize twice a week, sit where it can be read in a second.

Observations. The facts are all there, the airline, the start date and the days of the week, and the caption backs them up. The plane is the hero and Belize is nowhere in the frame, so the post looks like an airline advert on a tourism board's feed. Royal blue, orange and a small white box pull against the brand's own teal and mango palette, and the key facts sit in the smallest type on the post.

The remake. Frankfurt to the Blue Hole. Europe is now closer to Belize. Discover Airlines, Thursdays and Sundays, 16 December 2027 to mid April 2028. Photo, The Great Blue Hole from the air, by Agnes Lee on Unsplash.

What changed. The place is the hero. The Blue Hole fills the frame. Nobody books Belize for the aircraft, so the plane became one small icon on the boarding pass. The facts read like a ticket. Airport codes, the airline, the days and the season sit in one boarding pass block at the bottom, in the order someone checks them. The brand's own colours. Teal, mango and sand from the Belize brand replace the royal blue and orange, so the post looks like the board and the website.

Strategy. Audience, Travellers in Germany and the rest of Europe planning a winter escape, and the travel agents and press who cover new routes. Pillars, The place, one aerial or underwater frame a week with the flight as a line of small type. The route, boarding pass posts for every seasonal service with dates, days and the airline. The first week, what to do in Belize between landing on a Thursday and flying home on a Sunday. Rhythm, Four posts a week, two epic frames, one route or practical post and one Reel from the water, every one with the same boarding pass block for facts. Target, Saves and shares on route posts, and clicks through to the airline's booking page from the link in bio, both tracked for 90 days.

The caption in the brand's voice. Frankfurt to the Blue Hole, twice a week. From 16 December 2027 Discover Airlines flies Frankfurt to Belize on Thursdays and Sundays, through mid April 2028. Land on Thursday, dive the Blue Hole on Friday, fly home with a tan on Sunday. Save this for the winter you have been promising yourself, and tag the person you would bring.

Month one. Build one boarding pass template for route posts in the brand's teal and mango, with slots for the codes, the days and the season. Pull the twenty best aerial and underwater photos the board already owns, cropped to 4 by 5 with room for one line of type. Agree a posting plan with Discover Airlines so both accounts post the route on the same day with the same facts.

### Episode 2. What if Aurora Expeditions posted like this?

How an expedition operator could make its impact number the one people remember. Brand Aurora Expeditions (@aurora_expeditions), DMC or tour operator, Australia. Original post https://www.instagram.com/p/DeXCZTNiNVy/ with 21 likes on 54,000 followers. Page https://pratimnarayan.com/whatif/aurora/

The post as it was. Kelp floating on dark water at dusk, shot from above, with the words We've planted 3,724 bathtubs full of kelp in cream serif type over the top left.

Style tested. Documentary and wildlife. Aurora sells real encounters with wild places, and its impact work is real too. Documentary and wildlife shows the kelp forest from inside, in the light, the way an expedition guest would see it, and lets the numbers read like field notes rather than a maths puzzle.

Inspired by Cristina Mittermeier and Paul Nicklen, which make conservation numbers land by putting the viewer inside the habitat first.

The big idea. Show the forest the money grows, lead with the number that is true and big, 17,300 plants, and translate the area into something a board and a guest can picture, about sixteen tennis courts.

Observations. The impact is real, measured and funded by guests, which is a story most operators would love to have. Kelp shot from above at dusk reads as murk at feed size, so the photo hides the thing the post is about. Bathtubs are hard to picture and the caption's stronger facts, the area restored and the partner, never make it onto the image.

The remake. 17,300 kelp plants, back in the sea. 46,554 square feet of ocean habitat restored on the Sunshine Coast, about 16 tennis courts of forest, funded by every Aurora passenger. Planted with veritree. Photo, A kelp forest lit from above, photographed at Catalina, by Erick Morales Oyola on Unsplash.

What changed. The forest, from inside. A kelp forest in the light replaces the murky top down shot, so the post shows the habitat the number is about. The true number leads. 17,300 plants is the fact. The bathtub maths is gone, and the area becomes sixteen tennis courts, which anyone can picture. The caption's facts on the image. The square feet, the coast, the partner and the line that every passenger funds it moved from the caption onto the post.

Strategy. Audience, Travellers in Australia, the US and the UK who book expedition cruises a year out and care where the money goes, plus the agents who sell them. Pillars, Inside the habitat, one frame a week from the water, the ice or the deck with the guide's own note. The impact ledger, one number per post with a comparison a guest can picture. The voyage, what a day looks like on board, told by the expedition team. Rhythm, Four posts a week, two documentary frames, one impact number and one Reel from the expedition team, with the impact number repeated in every voyage caption. Target, Saves and shares on impact posts, and enquiries that mention the kelp or the voyage programme, tracked for 90 days.

The caption in the brand's voice. 17,300 kelp plants, back in the sea. With veritree we have restored 46,554 square feet of ocean habitat on the Sunshine Coast of British Columbia, about sixteen tennis courts of forest, and every Aurora passenger helped pay for it. Kelp forests store carbon, shelter fish and come back fast when someone plants them. Save this if you want to see where your voyage goes, and ask us anything about the programme in the comments.

Month one. Ask veritree for the project's own photos and the restoration map, so the next impact post is the real site. Write a one line comparison for every impact number before it is posted, so no guest has to do maths. Put the impact number and a tracked link in every voyage post caption for 90 days and count the saves.

### Episode 3. What if PARKROYAL posted like this?

How a hotel group could sell a spa offer with the one view only it has. Brand PARKROYAL Hotels and Resorts (@parkroyalhotels), Hotel or resort, Singapore. Original post https://www.instagram.com/p/Dd_DbW6Fs6x/ with 3 likes on 13,000 followers. Page https://pratimnarayan.com/whatif/parkroyal/

The post as it was. A spa therapist giving a massage beside an arched window with palms outside, and a large white Pan Pacific DISCOVERY frame and logo covering the top third of the photo.

Style tested. Quiet luxury. A member spa offer is a quiet luxury message, and PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering has a view no other hotel in Singapore can post, the sky garden pool. Quiet luxury sets the photo with air around it, one serif line and the offer as a single number, so the frame feels like the hotel instead of a loyalty programme notice.

Inspired by Four Seasons, which makes an offer feel like an invitation by naming the property and letting one photo carry it.

The big idea. Name the hotel, show the garden that makes it famous, and turn the loyalty frame into one line of small type and one big number, 25%, so the offer is the easiest thing on the post to read.

Observations. The spa photo is warm and well lit, and the offer behind it is genuinely good. A loyalty programme frame covers a third of the photo, so the post reads as a notice from head office rather than a hotel. No property is named and the offer lives only in the caption, so a follower has to work to find out what is on offer and where.

The remake. Your massage comes with a garden. For Pan Pacific DISCOVERY members. Save up to 25% at participating spa outlets. Slow down, switch off and make room for a little me time on your next getaway. Photo, The sky garden pool at PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering, the hotel's own photograph, by Pan Pacific Hotels Group on panpacific.com.

What changed. A view only this hotel has. The sky garden pool at Pickering replaces a spa photo that could be any hotel anywhere, and the property is named under it. The offer as one number. 25% is the biggest thing on the post after the headline. The loyalty frame became one line of small type above it. Air around the photo. Cream margins, one serif line and the hotel's own logo, so the post looks like the hotel rather than a programme announcement.

Strategy. Audience, Business and weekend travellers in Singapore, Australia and across Asia who already hold a Pan Pacific DISCOVERY membership, and the ones one stay away from joining. Pillars, The view only we have, one frame a week from a named property, with the hour it was taken. The member offer, one number, one property, one line, in the same quiet frame every time. The people, a therapist, a gardener or a chef, named, once every ten posts. Rhythm, Three posts a week, two quiet frames from named properties and one member offer, with the loyalty sign up link in the first comment. Target, Member sign ups and spa bookings traced to the link in bio and the first comment, aiming to grow both every month for 90 days.

The caption in the brand's voice. Your massage comes with a garden. Pan Pacific DISCOVERY members save up to 25% at participating spa outlets, and at PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering that means St. Gregory on Level 5, with 15,000 square metres of sky gardens outside the treatment room. Not a member yet. The link in bio takes a minute. Tag the person who needs this more than you do.

Month one. Collect one signature photo per property, the view only that hotel has, and crop each one to 4 by 5 with room for a line. Build the quiet offer template once, cream margins, one serif headline, one number, and use it for every member offer. Confirm which spa outlets take part in the offer and name the property on every offer post from now on.

### Episode 4. What if GSTC posted like this?

How the council that writes the standard could fill a free training day in Bangkok. Brand GSTC (@gstcouncil), Tourism association, Global. Original post https://www.instagram.com/p/DerMcyQo8LO/ with 5 likes on 5,900 followers. Page https://pratimnarayan.com/whatif/gstc/

The post as it was. A landscape graphic with cartoon characters and coloured tiles on the left in Agoda's palette, and on the right the course title in purple with a date and a venue underneath.

Style tested. Photo poster. A dated course with a venue is a poster job, and a photo poster done well is the format. A real traveller in a real place says more about accessibility than cartoon blobs, and the three facts that fill a room, that it is free, that it is one day and who is teaching, go in big type and a clean strip at the bottom.

Inspired by London Marathon, which sells a date with one photo of a real person, one line and the facts in a strip.

The big idea. Lead with the three words that fill a free course, Free, One day, Bangkok, show a traveller who uses a wheelchair in a place worth travelling to, and give the trainer and the venue the strip at the bottom.

Observations. The date and the venue are on the post, and the partnership with Agoda is a real advantage. Cartoon characters in a partner's palette make a professional course look like a children's app, and the landscape format shows up small in the feed. The fee waiver and the trainer, the two facts most likely to get someone to register, are hidden in the caption.

The remake. Free. One day. Bangkok. Learn to welcome the 1 in 6 people who live with a disability. Monday 23 November at the Agoda One Bangkok office, with trainer Martin Heng, Lonely Planet's former Accessible Travel Manager. Fee waived with Agoda's support. Photo, A woman in a wheelchair on the rim of the Grand Canyon, by Romain Virtuel on Unsplash.

What changed. Three words that fill a room. Free, one day and Bangkok are the reasons someone registers, so they became the headline instead of the course's formal title. A real traveller, a real place. A woman in a wheelchair on the canyon rim replaces the cartoon tiles, and the post is 4 by 5 so it fills the feed on a phone. The facts in a strip. When, where and who teaches it sit in one clean strip with both logos, and the fee waiver moved from the caption onto the post.

Strategy. Audience, Hotel general managers, front office and operations leads in Thailand and Southeast Asia, and the sustainability officers who choose which courses their teams attend. Pillars, The course, one poster per date with the fact that fills the room in the headline. The standard in practice, one certified property and one accessible feature, photographed as it is. The trainer and the graduates, who taught it and what they changed afterwards. Rhythm, Three posts a week, one course poster, one from a certified property and one from a trainer or graduate, every course post with a tracked registration link. Target, Registrations traced from social for each course, aiming to double social's share of seats within 90 days.

The caption in the brand's voice. Free. One day. Bangkok. On Monday 23 November GSTC runs its first accessibility and inclusion training for hospitality teams in Thailand, at the Agoda One Bangkok office, with Martin Heng, who led accessible travel at Lonely Planet for seven years. Over 1.3 billion people live with a disability, about 1 in 6 of us, and most hotels still make them do the work. The fee is waived with Agoda's support. Seats are limited, so register at gstc.org and tag a colleague who should be in the room.

Month one. Build one photo poster template in the council's green with a strip for when, where and who, and use it for every dated course. License ten photographs of real travellers with disabilities in real places, so no course post needs a cartoon again. Put the fee waiver and the trainer on the post itself every time, and add a tracked registration link to every course caption.

### Episode 5. What if IBTM World posted like this?

How a trade show could recruit buyers with the offer it already makes. Brand IBTM World (@ibtmevents), Travel media and events, Europe. Original post https://www.instagram.com/p/Deei6J5iGca/ with 5 likes on 16,000 followers. Page https://pratimnarayan.com/whatif/ibtm/

The post as it was. A square photo of a visitor standing inside a red and silver geodesic stand with Toronto branding and QR codes, under a blue to pink gradient wash, with the words Inspiration for every event planner and a pale blue Apply Now button.

Style tested. Text hook overlay. IBTM's Hosted Buyer programme pays for your flight and your hotel, which is one of the strongest hooks in the whole events industry, and the post never says it. Text hook overlay puts that line in big type over Barcelona from the air, in the brand's electric blue, so the scroll stops on the offer.

Inspired by VisitScotland, which stops the scroll with one line of big type over a real view and keeps the details for the caption.

The big idea. Say the thing that gets a buyer to apply, your flight to Barcelona is on us, over the city itself, and keep the dates, the venue and the stars in one line underneath.

Observations. The programme behind the post is excellent, free flights and a 4 or 5 star hotel for qualified buyers, and the dates are close enough to act on. The headline is generic and the hook sits in the caption, so the one line that would make a planner apply is the one line nobody sees. The photo shows another city's stand with its own branding and QR codes, under a gradient wash and a pale web style button that does nothing on Instagram.

The remake. Your flight to Barcelona is on us. Qualify as a Hosted Buyer and we cover your return flight and a 4 or 5 star hotel. Your three days go on the business. IBTM World, 17 to 19 November 2026, Fira Barcelona Gran Via. Photo, Barcelona's Eixample and the Sagrada Familia from the air, by Rockwell branding agency on Unsplash.

What changed. The hook is the headline. Your flight to Barcelona is on us was buried in the caption. Now it is the biggest thing on the post, in the brand's electric blue. Barcelona, not Toronto. The city the show is in replaces another city's stand, and the gradient wash is gone so the photo can do its job. One line of details. The hotel, the dates and the venue sit in one line under the hook, with a button that says where to apply instead of a fake web button.

Strategy. Audience, Corporate and agency event planners in Europe, North America and the Gulf who place business in Spain and the Mediterranean, and the association planners who bring congresses. Pillars, The offer, one hook per post about what Hosted Buyers get, over Barcelona. The people, exhibitors and buyers who met at the show and what they booked. The city, three days in Barcelona for a planner, told like a guide. Rhythm, Four posts a week until the show, two hooks, one story from a past buyer and one Barcelona Reel, each with the application link in the first comment. Target, Hosted Buyer applications traced to social through the tracked link, and the share of applications that come from Instagram versus email, measured weekly until 17 November.

The caption in the brand's voice. Your flight to Barcelona is on us. Qualify as a Hosted Buyer for IBTM World and we cover your return flight and a 4 or 5 star hotel, so your three days go on the business. 17 to 19 November 2026 at Fira Barcelona Gran Via, with thousands of exhibitors and the planners who place the biggest events in the world. Applications close soon. The link in the first comment takes four minutes, and tag the planner on your team who should be there.

Month one. Write ten hooks from the Hosted Buyer terms, one benefit each, and run them over Barcelona photography until the show. Replace every web style button in the template with a line that says where the link is, and put the tracked link in the first comment every time. Interview three past Hosted Buyers for a story post each, with what they booked at the show.

## Questions people ask

- What's in the free audit? Your website, social media, email and search, each scored out of 10 and explained in plain English. Then the three fixes worth doing first. It's written, so you can forward it to your board or owner without me in the room.
- Is it really free? What's the catch? It's free. Some people read it and ask me to do the fixes. Plenty don't, and that's fine. You won't be added to a list or chased.
- Is it only social media? No. Social builds attention, but email is where people actually book, register and join. I run both, and connect them with tracked links so you can see which posts lead to real enquiries.
- How will I show my board it's working? With one page a month. For associations that means member signups, event registrations and newsletter growth. For DMCs and operators, enquiries and bookings traced from posts and emails. For hotels, direct booking clicks against the OTAs, plus revenue from email offers.
- What does it cost to work together? It depends on how many posts and platforms you need. Plans are built around your budget, so share yours in the form and I'll suggest a scope that fits. The free week and the audit cost nothing.
- You're in India and we're in the US or Europe. Will that work? ATTA is in the US and PATA is in Bangkok, and I worked remotely with both. WFTA's network spans more than 150 countries. I plan around your working hours and reply within one working day.
- Is it really just you? Yes. I write your audit, plan the calendar, make the posts and walk you through the numbers myself, every month.
- Is it safe to hire a marketer based in India? PATA, ATTA and the World Food Travel Association have trusted me with their work. Every project starts with a free week or a free audit, so you see the work before you pay, and paid work runs on a signed agreement.
- How do time zones work with my team? I work from India. For US clients, posts and replies are ready before your morning. For European clients, our afternoons overlap, and that's when we talk.
- What happens after my free week? You get the 5 posts, a short walkthrough video and a one page plan for the next 90 days. If you want me to keep going, we start the next month. If not, the posts are yours.
- Will I approve every post before it goes live? Yes. You see each week's posts before they're scheduled, and nothing goes live without your approval.
- Can I pause in my low season? Yes. Tell me 15 days ahead and we pause until your season starts again.
- Do I keep the posts? Yes. The 5 posts and their captions are yours whether or not we work together, in files you can upload to your own accounts.
- What happens after the free week? You get the posts, a short walkthrough video and a one page plan for the next 90 days. If you want me to keep going, we start the next month. If not, the posts are yours and we part as friends.
- Who does the work? I do. I plan and design every post myself, write the captions and record the walkthrough. Nothing is handed to a junior or a tool you haven't met.

## The twelve visual styles the series tests

- 01 Quiet luxury. Calm frames with few or no people, where space and light do the selling. Best for Luxury resorts and heritage hotels, wellness retreats and private villas. Watch out, Without a human story the feed goes cold. One face every ten posts keeps it warm.
- 02 Editorial glamour. Art directed scenes with styled people, shot like a fashion or travel magazine. Best for Heritage hotels and palaces, luxury trains and cruises, airlines with a cabin story and fashion led stays. Watch out, Generic styling dates fast. Keep one recurring character or uniform so the look stays yours.
- 03 Epic scenery. Big views at golden hour, from the air or the edge, with a person for scale at most. Best for Tourism boards, trekking operators, adventure brands and DMCs selling mountains or coastline. Watch out, This is the most crowded lane in travel. Every destination looks alike at sunset, so pair it with a hook or a human story.
- 04 Moody atmosphere. Weather as a feature. Mist, rain, night skies and low light sell how the place feels. Best for Himalayan and Northeast India destinations, monsoon campaigns, cabins and nature lodges, and slow travel brands. Watch out, Too much darkness in a row reads as sad. Break it with one bright frame a week.
- 05 Documentary and wildlife. Real moments caught as they happen, from wildlife sightings to guides and locals at work. Best for Safari lodges, expedition cruises, cultural and community tourism, responsible travel brands and associations. Watch out, Staged documentary reads fake straight away. If the access is not real, pick another style.
- 06 Warm lifestyle. People enjoying the place in warm light, candid but polished. Best for Lifestyle and boutique hotels, resorts, restaurants and hotel food and drink, and group tour operators. Watch out, Without a real story it slides into stock photography. Shoot actual moments, then edit hard.
- 07 Creator led. A face talking to camera, or a phone held up in the moment. Best for Hostels, OTAs, youth and group tour operators, and destinations working with creators. Watch out, The account is only as good as its presenter, and brand control drops. Agree on guardrails before the first shoot.
- 08 Text hook overlay. Real footage with one line of text on top that makes people stop scrolling. Best for Tourism boards chasing reach, OTAs, tour operators with lists and tips, and any account that needs saves. Watch out, Clickbait hooks with weak payoffs burn trust. The slide after the hook has to deliver.
- 09 Bold graphic. Designed posts where typography and brand colour lead. Best for Associations and trade bodies, OTAs, publishers, award news, itineraries and B2B travel. Watch out, Text heavy posts earn saves but travel less on their own. Keep a photo or one big number as the hero of each frame.
- 10 Meme and pop culture. Humour and culture moments, posted while they are still fresh. Best for Indian state boards, budget airlines, hostels, youth brands and any client with a bold voice. Watch out, Risky for luxury, and jokes age quickly. Write a tone guide with clear no go topics before the first post.
- 11 Signature colour and retro. One strict visual rule repeated until the feed is recognisable at a glance. Best for Boutique and design hotels, cafes, heritage brands with archives and any client that needs to stand out in a crowded grid. Watch out, A rule that is too narrow wears thin. Pick one you can feed every single week.
- 12 Photo poster. A photo with the brand logo and a headline, the format most tourism accounts post every day. Best for Event announcements, offers and anything with a date, when the photo is strong and the text is short. Watch out, Three fonts, two logos and a sponsor strip turn a poster into noise. One headline, one logo, one action.
